turns.t: Hi, sorry, I probably shouldn't have come in, it's nothing, my heart just did a thing at work.
He's the one who got the manager to call a cab, doctor. Tell her what you told me. ~
Come on in, take a seat. What did your heart do?
It started racing, thumping really, and I felt kind of light-headed. I thought I was about to go down.
And how long did that last?
Maybe ten minutes? Honestly I wasn't looking at a clock, I was gripping the printer.
Has it ever happened before?
Hmm. I think so, a while back, but I can't tell you when. Might've been last spring, might've been the winter before.
I took a note of how long he was sitting out there. About forty minutes, and he was fine the whole time. ~
Good to know, thank you. Is it still going on now?
No, it settled while I was waiting. I just feel a bit wrung out, you know?
That's understandable. Anything else going on with you lately, big stress, not much sleep? ~
Work's been crazy since the merger, and I've been living on coffee to keep up. I know, I know. ~
That's probably not helping you. It's worth cutting down, and I'll tell you why in a second. ~
I figured you'd say that. Is my heart okay? ~
What you describe sounds like it settled by itself, and that's reassuring. I don't want to over-read a single episode, though. ~
So what happens now? ~
Honestly, today is mostly advice. Cut the coffee down to one or two a day, and drink water at your desk, especially when you're busy.
I can give you a leaflet on what to do if it happens again. ~
That'd be great. I'm terrible at remembering things when I'm panicking. ~
The leaflet will say it simply. If it comes back, sit down, breathe slowly, and time it.
Sit and time it. Okay. What if it doesn't stop? ~
If it lasts more than twenty minutes, or you get chest pain, or you actually faint, call for an ambulance. Don't drive yourself.
Right. Okay. I think I've got it. ~
I'll go and fetch that leaflet now, and I'll find you some water while I'm at it. ~
Thank you both. Sorry again for taking up your time. ~
You haven't, and you were right to come. Look after yourself. ~
Back in a minute. ~
Take care, doctor. ~
And you. ~
Right, back to the printer. ~
Maybe sit down first. ~

chief_complaint.value: my heart just did a thing at work

clinical_actions.description: Advise cutting caffeine and drinking water
Advise to sit, breathe slowly and time any recurrence
Safety-net: call ambulance if over 20 minutes, chest pain or fainting

clinical_uncertainties.description: Patient could not say when a previous similar episode occurred ("last spring, might've been the winter before").
